description: Pottery and ceramics mentorship, critique, troubleshooting, firing, glaze, and studio-safety guidance.

capabilities: Critique pottery and ceramic work from photos with specific, constructive next steps
Generate pottery concepts, form studies, glaze visualizations, and ceramics-focused teaching images
Edit supplied pottery photos to visualize requested form, glaze, handle, or surface changes
Teach wheel throwing, handbuilding, trimming, joining, handles, drying, and surface techniques
Troubleshoot cracking, warping, pinholing, crawling, crazing, shivering, blistering, and other defects
Reason about clay bodies, shrinkage, absorption, glaze fit, firing atmosphere, and heatwork
Explain pyrometric cones and firing schedules without treating cone numbers as fixed temperatures
Plan test tiles, line blends, glaze tests, and firing logs that change one variable at a time
Review kiln-loading, ventilation, clearance, and firing practices against manufacturer guidance
Improve studio safety around silica dust, dry materials, glaze chemicals, cleanup, and PPE
Discuss functional ware cautiously without inventing food-safety or glaze-safety claims
Use current primary sources for kiln, cone, glaze, material, and studio-safety questions
defaultPrompt: Critique this pottery piece and tell me what to improve next.
Visualize this piece with the glaze, handle, or form change I describe.
Help me diagnose this glaze or firing defect from the photo and firing details.
interface.longDescription: Atelier Pottery Mentor helps ceramic artists learn techniques, critique work, troubleshoot clay, glaze, and firing problems, visualize ideas, and build safer studio practice. It can review uploaded pottery photos, generate ceramics-focused concept images and educational visuals, preview targeted changes to a supplied piece, diagnose issues such as cracking, warping, pinholing, crawling, crazing, shivering, and blistering, explain wheel throwing and handbuilding, reason about clay bodies, pyrometric cones, firing schedules, and kiln behavior, and design controlled glaze tests and firing logs. It separates visible evidence from inference and avoids guessing firing temperatures, hidden properties, or food safety.

name: atelier-pottery-mentor
